verdicts.evidence: The logbook only runs simulation experiments on synthetic data testing single-quantile (τ=0.5) coefficient-function RMSE, not multi-quantile prediction precision on real kidney transplant data; the real-data UNOS/OPTN experiments are explicitly noted as not reproducible due to private data access.

The simulation shows interaction-aware models reduce coefficient RMSE by 58–85% versus Z-agnostic models in synthetic data with generic covariates, structurally supporting the interaction concept, but using a simplified LP estimator rather than the neural network, generic covariates rather than donor type/age, and no clinical significance assessment.

overall: The logbook runs CPU simulation experiments with a simplified linear-program censored quantile estimator (not the FunCQNet neural network) on synthetic data, showing interaction-aware models reduce coefficient RMSE by 58–85% versus Z-agnostic models. The real-data kidney transplant claims are not addressed because UNOS/OPTN data is access-controlled and no code was released by the authors.
